luca r.: Quick question We had a group shuttle to/from the conference booked through ShuttleGo app. The booking confirmation is an e-ticket that lists only a total and a booking ref (no per-person line items or VAT). I paid with my personal card and need to split between 4 attendees. How should we submit this so Finance can reimburse each person?
zara t.: Do you have the passenger list on the confirmation? If yes, upload the e-ticket and a short note listing the 4 names and who paid which share. We typically accept a single claim with attachments and then split it internally.
luca r.: The e-ticket shows passenger names but it's not broken out by price. Total was $96.50. I split equally with Venmo after the trip but Venmo isn't on company policy for settlement. Can I still claim $24.12 each?
people-ops: Venmo is OK for informal repayment between employees, but Finance prefers a single reimbursement going to the person who paid the vendor (you). Best approach: submit an expense for the full $96.50 on your reimbursement tool, attach: 1) ShuttleGo e-ticket, 2) screenshot of rider list, 3) a one-paragraph attestation naming the 3 colleagues who reimbursed you and the amounts they sent, 4) proof of transfers (Venmo screenshots) if available. Then mark the reimbursement as "split - internal recoverable" and finance will create internal allocations to charge back each attendee's cost to their next expense run.
michael p.: If one of the attendees wants to claim separately (they paid you back in cash), is there a way to avoid duplicate reimbursements?
finance-bot: Automated rule: If an expense is marked "split-recoverable" and supporting attachments include payer receipts or internal payment proof, Finance will process one payment to the payee and generate internal ledger entries to allocate the cost. Do NOT submit separate identical vendor claims for the same shuttle. If someone paid you back in cash and they want reimbursement instead of allocation, attach a signed attestation from both parties and Finance will treat it as a reimbursement reversal.
zara t.: One more thing Some countries require VAT invoices for VAT reclaim. If ShuttleGo cannot provide itemized VAT, flag it in the expense and Finance will mark it as non-reclaimable VAT. That won't prevent reimbursement, but VAT won't be recovered.
luca r.: Got it. I'll upload the e-ticket, Venmo screenshots, and a short attestation naming everyone. I'll mark it split in Expensify and tag @finance. Thanks! :+1:
finance-bot: Received ticket #FIN-4853. Expect allocation confirmation in 2-4 business days. If any attendee needs direct cash reimbursement instead of ledger allocation, reply here with their name and proof of payment.
people-ops: We'll add a sample "group-shuttle attestation" template to the travel FAQ (two-line template: "I, [payer], confirm I paid [vendor] $[total] for [date]; [names] reimbursed me $[amount] each via [method].")
